public.title: Dandelion pilot
public.hero: Menstrual-health products, delivered through trusted local people, paid with mobile money.

steps.1: An approved supplier prepares a sealed batch.
steps.2: A verified delivery partner pays with mobile money and collects it. The payment is confirmed by the mobile-money provider, never by a screenshot.
steps.3: The hub inspects and stores the stock, then sells to trained local sellers.
steps.4: Customers pay in full or in voluntary installments. No credit, no late fees, no debt.
steps.5: The product is handed over only after full confirmed payment, with a receipt.

public.ledgerHonest: Each day we publish a fingerprint of our records to a public ledger. Anyone with a receipt link can check that a record has not been changed since it was recorded. This does not prove the event itself was true — our checks against the payment provider's statements do that. Nothing is guaranteed by a blockchain.
public.statsNote: Weekly aggregate counts only. Small counts are shown as "fewer than 10" to protect privacy.
public.safetyDraft: DRAFT — requires review by a qualified health advisor
public.safetyReusable: Reusable products are offered only where the customer has access to clean water, soap, privacy, a place to wash, a place to dry products thoroughly, and safe storage. Reusable materials must be washed and dried after use.
public.safetyDisposable: Disposable products are offered where reusables are unsuitable because of water scarcity, lack of privacy, poor washing or drying conditions, or customer preference. Local sellers explain safe use and disposal.
public.safetySource: Source: pilot handbook §11, citing UNICEF guidance on menstrual hygiene products.

verify.honest: A match proves the record has not changed since it was anchored. It does not, by itself, prove the event happened. Payments are also checked monthly against the mobile-money provider's statements.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.p1: We collect your name or preferred name, phone number, product choice and payment status to manage your purchase and send receipts or reminders.
privacy.p2: We do not collect menstrual-cycle details, diagnoses, pregnancy status, sexual history or your exact home location.
privacy.p3: Your phone number is stored encrypted. Records are fingerprinted and the fingerprint is published to a public ledger; your identity is never published.
privacy.p4: We do not sell your information. Your data may be processed on servers outside Tanzania; this arrangement is being assessed under Tanzanian data-protection requirements before launch.
privacy.p5: You can ask us to correct your information, stop reminders, or delete your data. Contact {phone}.

map.title: District map
map.tickedHour: One hour of activity simulated through the real services.
map.tickedDay: One day of activity simulated through the real services, then reconciliation and anchoring.
map.legend: Left to right: factory · delivery partners · hubs, with their local sellers' kiosks and their customers underneath · organisations and customers served directly. Solid lines are the handbook ladder, dashed lines direct paths; grey pending · green confirmed · amber in review · red on hold. Every open order is a marker — a motorbike when a delivery partner carries it, a parcel otherwise — sitting where the order is: at the sender's door, on the road, or at the receiver's door; its ring is its payment colour and the number beside it is the units. A coin on a corner is money the provider confirmed to that place in the last hour. A padlock is a locked lot; a triangle a tile the attention chip points at. Click any place to see what it holds, what is coming and going, and its money. Customers are dots and counts, never names.
